arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Green argued that returning the property satisfies the restitution requirement under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act.
Ms. Harrington argued that the bank loses the difference between the loan amount and the property value.
Justice Kennedy asked if the property is fully returned when its value is less than the loan.
Justice Ginsburg asked how courts determine the property value at the time of foreclosure.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests how courts calculate restitution for mortgage fraud. the side that brought the case argues that returning the property satisfies the debt. The government argues that the bank loses the difference between the loan and the property value.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the court to rule that returning the property fully offsets the restitution order.
The government wants the court to rule that the bank must recover the difference between the loan and the property value.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that Section 3663A requires an offset when any part of the property is returned to the victim.
The government argues that the bank suffers a loss equal to the difference between the loan amount and the property value.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines how courts calculate restitution for mortgage fraud. It affects the financial recovery of banks and the liability of borrowers. The outcome sets a standard for valuing returned property in fraud cases.
